_about: Shared rule cases for the 008 tables and single-question rules, read by BOTH the backend tests (clean_rows / _validate_field_values) and the frontend tests (lib/form-checks.ts) so the wizard and filing cannot drift (008, FR-21 and FR-30). This is a SIBLING of deliverable_rows_cases.json (007), which is not edited; M1-M12 and F1-F2 are 007's, M9b, M13, M14, F3 and F4 are 008's.
Do not hand-edit casually: every `error` string is a message frozen in plan.md ('Interface freeze', 'Rules and exact messages'); change them only with the plan.

Each case names its form and question; the question definition (columns, limits, rules, labels) is read from backend/app/intake/agreement_forms.json, never copied here. Labels in messages come from the same form: 'Start date', 'End date' (the due-date window) and 'Will data leave India?' (the sub-processor country rule).

SECTION `tables`: one case per table check on the four new tables: new_agreement.consultancy_deliverables (Deliverables), new_agreement.key_individuals (Consultant's key individuals), dpa.transfer_countries (Countries outside India) and dpa.subprocessor_rows (Sub-processors).

id     = unique name across both sections; ok-* ids are accepted, m<N>-* ids are refused with that message (m9b = M9b), f<N>-* (in `fields`) with F<N>, num-* with the existing type message 'Field "{label}" must be a number' (_coerce_field).

values = the form's other answers the table rules read: start_date and end_date (the due-date window: both are days = M9; start is a day and end is not (missing, null, blank or not a day) = no end date, so only the start bound applies, M9b; start is not a day = no bound at all), transfer (the sub-processor country rule applies only while it is 'No'). A key left out means the answer is missing.
rows   = the raw answer exactly as sent (an array of row objects for most cases; a string, an object or a number for M1). Cells may be strings, numbers or null.
error  = the exact FIRST message, or null when accepted. The server raises the first problem; the wizard lists all of them in the same order, so rowsProblems(...)[0].message must equal `error`.
stored = (only when error is null) the cleaned answer: non-empty rows, tidied, shown-column keys only, in sent order. [] never occurs: an empty result is M3.

Row numbers in messages are 1-based positions in `rows` as sent, counting rows that are ignored because they are empty. Cells are tidied first (runs of ASCII whitespace become one space, ends trimmed; a no-break space is NOT whitespace here) and lengths count code points.

A one-column table (key individuals, countries) can never give M5: a row whose only cell is empty is ignored. A missing/blank answer (null or '') is NOT a case here: the filing validator treats it as 'required' before clean_rows runs.

Order inside one cell: required (M5), length (M6), blank bracket (M7), then 'India' (M13), then the Country must be India (M14); dates: form (M8), then the window (M9, or M9b with no end date). Rows are checked top to bottom, columns left to right, THEN the repeats (M11).

SECTION `fields`: the single-question rules F1 (no_blanks), F2 (min_exclusive), F3 (max_length) and F4 (max_decimals), run after the question's own type check (a number question that is not a number gets the existing type message). `values` = the other answers the question's `show` and `rules_when` read (every case is for a SHOWN question); `value` = the answer after JSON decoding (a string, as the wizard sends it, or a JSON number, as an API client may; a test that needs text reads String(value)); `error` = the exact server message or null when accepted. The wizard words F1-F4 from the verb (Is longer than 120 characters. / Can have at most 2 decimal places.) so the TypeScript test compares them with the label and full stop stripped; it must agree on refused vs accepted for every case.

Order inside one question: F3 (length, after tidying), F1 (brackets), F2 (above the floor), F4 (decimals). F4 is judged on the answer as typed (commas removed, ends trimmed): when that is not a plain ASCII number (^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ - so 1e3, .5, 5., +25, full-width and Arabic-Indic digits) the answer gets the existing 'must be a number' message (num-* ids) instead of F4, even if the server's own number parsing would have read it; when it is a plain number with more than 2 decimals it gets F4. A question with `rules_when` is judged by none of these unless every rule matches (Consultancy AND our paper; the DPA purpose: our paper).
Non-ASCII characters are written as \u escapes on purpose (a no-break space, a full-width digit or an emoji is invisible or look-alike in an editor).
